subject: Enable Stratix ACH + confirm invoice remittance payload
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena@stratixsystems.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-20T09:02:00Z
Subject: Stratix payment setup docs and invoice sample

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the onboarding call this morning. Per our checklist, attached are the bank authorization form, a completed W-9, and a voided check for the account we'll use for ACH and wires. I've also attached a sample invoice showing the remittance payload fields we include from our billing system.

Quick notes:
- Bank: First Harbor Commercial
- Routing: 011000015
- Account: 4287654321 (Stratix Systems, operating account)
- Remittance field we prefer: remit_id (third-party reference), PO number, and invoice_line_item ids

Attachments: Stratix_BankAuth_Form.pdf, Stratix_W9.pdf, voided_check.jpg, Stratix_invoice_sample.xlsx

Let me know if you need the bank letter instead of the voided check — we can request one from our bank.

Best,
Elena Ruiz
Head of Finance Operations
Stratix Systems
elena@stratixsystems.com
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@stratixsystems.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-20T11:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Stratix payment setup docs and invoice sample

Elena — thanks, received all four attachments and skimmed the sample invoice. A few quick items before we flip this to Finance for activation:

1) PO mapping: our payments team requires the PO number be supplied in the invoice metadata as either PO_NUM or as a top-line invoice field called "Purchase Order". Can you confirm where Stratix currently injects the PO? (we saw PO in a comment column in the sample file but want to be sure the single field exists in your invoice payload).

2) Remit string: your sample shows "remit_id" — good. Please include an explicit remit email or remittance string in the invoice PDF metadata if possible (some ERPs push this to the PDF metadata or to EDI mapping).

3) ACH prenote: Finance requires either a micro-deposit/ACH prenote or a bank letter. We can accept micro-deposits (typical) — does Stratix do a prenote flow or prefer a bank verification letter?

Next steps from our side: I'll open a procurement PO (STRAT-9853) and send a procurement portal link; Finance will take the bank docs and run a prenote if you confirm micro-deposit is ok. If you can confirm the PO mapping and which verification path (micro-deposit vs letter) by EOD Tuesday we'll target activation by Friday.

Small ask: please include the remittance email address you want on the payment advice (we often include it for AP exceptions).

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Procurement Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

From: Victor Lane <victor.lane@stratixsystems.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@stratixsystems.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-21T08:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Stratix payment setup docs and invoice sample

Hi Soojin — thanks for the quick review.

Answers below:
- PO mapping: Our billing system writes the PO to the field PO_NUM (single-field) and it appears in the exported invoice CSV as PO_NUM. In the attached Stratix_invoice_sample.xlsx tab "export_example" you'll see the PO_NUM column populated. We'll also include the PO on the invoice PDF in the header.
- Remittance email: Please send payment advice to billing@stratixsystems.com
- Verification: We prefer micro-deposits. We will accept a micro-deposit prenote from Redwood and will confirm once received.

We also added a column with "remit_id" in the sample spreadsheet that maps to your remit_id requirement.

If you'd like a bank confirmation letter in addition to the voided check, we can request one — it will add 1–2 business days. Micro-deposit is fastest.

Best,
Victor Lane
Senior Accountant, Stratix Systems
victor.lane@stratixsystems.com

From: jordan_blake@redwood.com
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-21T15:06:00Z
Subject: Re: Stratix payment setup docs and invoice sample

Looping in for PO/GL coding — Soojin, when you create the PO STRAT-9853 can you tag it with GL: 5202 (SaaS vendor spend) and set payment terms Net 30? Finance also asks that the payee name on the banking record exactly match the payee on the PO (Stratix Systems vs Stratix, Inc.). Victor, can you confirm the legal entity name used on the bank account?

Also: will Stratix require any special reference when Redwood sends the ACH (we send ACH with trace number and sometimes include remittance text of up to 80 chars)? If so, send the preferred remittance snippet.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Procurement Analyst, Redwood Inference

From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: Victor Lane <victor.lane@stratixsystems.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@stratixsystems.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: 2028-06-22T16:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Stratix payment setup docs and invoice sample

Victor / Elena — all good, thanks for the confirmations. Final checklist summary:

- PO: STRAT-9853 created and visible in our procurement portal (link below). PO tagged GL: 5202 and Net 30.
- Payee name: please confirm legal name on bank account (reply inline).
- Micro-deposit: Finance will issue a nominal micro-deposit to 4287654321 by 2028-06-24 (expect $0.01–$0.25). Please confirm once you see it and reply with the exact cents so we can move to Live payments.
- Remittance: payment advice will be sent to billing@stratixsystems.com. ACH remittance text will contain: "RDWD PAY STRATIX | PO: {PO_NUM} | INV: {INV_NUM}" (80 char max). If you need a different snippet, tell us now.
- Attachments: bank auth, W9, voided check, invoice sample stored in Drive (Doc link below).

Doc links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3C4dStratixInvoiceSample
PO: https://procure.redwood.ai/po/STRAT-9853
Docusign (payment terms): https://docusign.com/embedded/sign/abc123-stratix-payment-terms

If we don't hear about the payee legal name mismatch, we'll assume it is "Stratix Systems" exactly as on the bank auth and proceed. Looking forward to first remittance test.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Procurement Manager
Redwood Inference
